name: Zayed Makandar

hero.tagline:
AI/ML Engineer.
I build vision, speech and LLM systems that hold up in the real world.

about.label: About
lines: I'm an AI/ML engineer based in Hubli, Karnataka, India.
I build intelligent systems that see, listen and understand language, then make them fast enough for the hardware people actually have.
A CPU-only server. One shared GPU. A kiosk in a noisy lobby.
When a system isn't fast or intelligent enough, I dig in: read the research, test the options, and keep what the benchmarks prove.
I also designed and taught an AI/ML curriculum, from classical ML to transformers, for trainers and students.

projects.label: Projects
projects._note: Items with "earlier": true are shown smaller, under the earlierLabel heading.

items.title: DocIntel
items.line: Turns PDFs, scans and Office files into clean Markdown, in 90+ languages.
items.description: A GPU microservice built around a 5B vision-language OCR model, with a switchable Transformers/vLLM backend, serving a multi-agent learning platform. Tuning batching, prefix caching and shared-GPU memory took a 10-page document from 95 s to 13.3 s.
items.imageAlt: Illustration of a document page being converted into structured Markdown

items.title: QuoteVision
items.line: Reads scanned vendor quotations and turns them into validated purchase-order data, on a CPU-only server.
items.description: A self-hosted 1B vision-language OCR model turns each page into Markdown tables, then deterministic code extracts and cross-checks the line items. Quantisation, NUMA pinning and image-token capping made it 3.47× faster, with 67% fewer visual tokens per page.
items.imageAlt: Illustration of a quotation document being turned into a validated table

items.title: Edge-AI Health Monitor
items.line: Offline health screening with sensors, a webcam and ten INT8 models on a CPU.
items.description: A multi-pathway PyTorch model (1D-CNN, wavelet 2D-CNN, LSTM, self-attention) feeds five risk modules, all quantised to INT8 ONNX: 601 KB in total and 0.71 ms per screening on a laptop CPU. A webcam module reads contactless heart rate (rPPG), blink rate and stress alongside IoT vital-sign sensors.
items.imageAlt: Illustration of an ECG trace on a grid

items.title: VoiceDesk
items.line: A voice receptionist that runs entirely on one local machine.
items.description: Local speech-to-text, RAG over an editable ChromaDB knowledge base, a local LLM and streamed speech replies. A wake-word fuzzy matcher and correction layer, built from real lobby logs, keeps it working in a noisy room, with automatic offline TTS fallback.
items.imageAlt: Illustration of an audio waveform next to a speech bubble

items.title: AIOS
items.line: A voice agent that qualifies sales leads in 11 Indian languages.
items.description: A real-time Pipecat pipeline with noise suppression, smart turn detection and code-mixed speech recognition. It opens in Kannada, follows the caller into their language, and turns every call into structured lead data.
items.imageAlt: Illustration of a phone call turning into a structured lead record

items.title: VoxServe
items.line: Self-hosted speech-to-text, LLM chat and text-to-speech behind one API for AR/VR institutes.
items.description: A multi-tenant FastAPI platform with role-based portals, per-key analytics and a Unity C# SDK. GPU work is queued, and every model falls back to the CPU automatically when the GPU runtime is missing.
items.imageAlt: Illustration of speech, text and audio flowing through one API

items.title: AIURVA
items.line: Concept for a multilingual AI health-intake kiosk.
items.description: Patients answer an adaptive interview in English, Hindi or Kannada. Speech is routed to Whisper or a Triton-served regional model, and a pre-consultation summary moves through doctor and lab review on one record.
items.imageAlt: Illustration of a kiosk interview in three languages

items.title: Assist
items.line: A voice-activated AI desktop assistant for Windows.
items.description: Wake word, speech recognition and GPT-4o, plus desktop actions: open apps, play Spotify or YouTube, check the weather and news. Built in May–June 2025 with PyQt.
items.imageAlt: Illustration of a chat window with a microphone

items.title: MusicalWorld
items.line: A music sharing site for independent singers.
items.description: Accounts with email verification, songs by language, user uploads, favourites and an admin panel, built with PHP and MySQL. Completed March 2024.
items.imageAlt: Illustration of a music player with an upload button

items.title: Tetris
items.line: Classic Tetris in Python and pygame.
items.description: A Computer Graphics course team project with three difficulty levels, a saved high score and animated menu screens. Completed July 2024.
